title: A 17-digit bank account number typed as a number is not turned into scientific notation
preconditions: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation).
steps: Bank Account Number = 12345678901234500 as a NUMBER cell
expectedResult: Staged value '12345678901234500' (or the row refused as not text). Rule: app/services/conversions/excel_to_json_conversion_service.rb:176.
rationale: Indian bank accounts run to 17 digits. Typed into Excel as a number, the cell reaches Roo as a Float, and Ruby prints a Float of 17+ digits as '1.23456789012345e+16' — that string is what gets stored. (Excel itself keeps only 15 significant digits, so the cell should be text; the product should refuse or warn rather than store scientific notation.)
